summary: The paper sharpens foundational constants in quantum randomness extraction and privacy amplification established by Regula and Cheng (2026). It presents three major contributions: Theorem A proves that the half-quadratic and fully-quadratic binary hypothesis-testing errors satisfy a tight universal constant of 25/16 = 1.5625 via an explicit spectral-clipping POVM and Loewner identity; Theorem B sharpens the 4*-universal one-shot leftover-hash converse constant from 1/3 to C_sharp(p) > 1/3 with an exact rational regime transition at p* = 1/8 and integer peak of 1/2 at |Z| = 4, 5; and Theorem C repairs a factor-of-2 scaling typo and retains |Z|-1 factors in strong-converse achievability bounds. All 22 theorems are machine-checked in constructive Lean 4.35.0 with zero sorry and zero custom axioms, accompanied by an AST-audited zero-float Python verifier and 16 JSON certificates.
weaknesses: The asymptotic p -> 0 behaviour and whether the 1/3 bottleneck in Haagerup-Musat truncation can be surpassed remain open problems.
The mathematical exposition is dense and assumes deep familiarity with noncommutative operator inequalities and quantum hypothesis testing.
